design.a: src/pages/api/matches/[id]/rewind-preview.ts - the preview arm captures the writer's return and answers {...result, privateRefs: {preview?: opaqueRef, reason?: opaqueRef}} (only refs that exist). Refusal arms (400/401/403/404/409) unchanged, so a refused caller still receives no ref and no row. The refs are opaque handles, never payloads; the read route re-authorizes every one of them. This route never passes privateReason today, so only `preview` can appear; the `reason` arm follows the writer's declared return contract
design.b: src/pages/api/matches/[id]/private-preview.ts (1 line) re-exports src/pages-modules/api/matchPrivatePreviewRoute.ts, exactly as export.ts and timeline.ts do
design.c: src/pages-modules/api/matchPrivatePreviewRoute.ts (new): prepareMatchHistoryGet -> `ref` via rejectMissingQueryString(req,res,'ref',...) (missing or non-string: 400 {error}) -> getDefaultMatchStore().getMatchMeta(caller.matchId) in its own try/catch (unknown match: 404 {error:'unknown match'}, the status the preview route answers) -> createViewerHistoryServiceOver(new HostAsGmMembershipSource(new MatchSeatMembershipSource(store), meta.hostPlayerId)).exportForViewer(caller.playerId, caller.matchId, {streamType: DEFAULT_MATCH_HISTORY_STREAM_TYPE, streamId: caller.matchId, includePrivate: true, occurredAt: nowIso(), privateRefs: [ref]}) -> res.status(200).json(body) VERBATIM (no lineage, no wrapper, nothing the service did not return) -> catch rejectMatchHistoryFailure(res, error, 'failed to read the private preview')
design.d: src/pages-modules/api/matchHistoryViewerChain.ts - the narrowest factory variant: the body of createViewerHistoryService() (:111-130) is lifted into an exported createViewerHistoryServiceOver(membership: IMembershipSource), and createViewerHistoryService() becomes a delegator that passes new MatchSeatMembershipSource(getDefaultMatchStore()). ONE service graph, one owner, and the privileged variant has a greppable name a privacy reviewer can find
design.deviationFromTheAddendum: the addendum asks that createViewerHistoryService() stay byte-identical. Its BODY is not byte-identical under design D (it becomes a 3-line delegation); its signature, its exported name, its production graph and every call site are unchanged, and the export/timeline route files are untouched. The alternative that keeps the bytes - a second factory that re-declares the same five dependencies - would create two copies of one service graph that can drift apart silently. Recorded here rather than decided silently
design.whatTheGmBodyCarries: IViewerHistoryExport verbatim: stream, timeline, privateRecords, timelineDigest. privateRecords is [{opaqueRef, payloadState, recordKind, payload}] for a ref of this match
design.whatThePlayerBodyCarries: the same four keys with privateRecords [{opaqueRef, payloadState, recordKind}] - no payload key anywhere - and the player-class stream and timeline, i.e. the same body the player's /export returns minus lineage and minus privateRecords

risksForTheParent: PRIVACY, and the single most reviewable thing on this head: the read route brands the match host as gm for the WHOLE export, not only for the private record. ViewerHistoryService.ts:144-161 resolves one viewer and uses it for the projection, the timeline and the private refs alike, so the GM's /private-preview body carries GM-class timeline rows (committedFirstRevision / committedLastRevision and every actor's principal id) that the same GM's /export body does not. This is a deliberate consequence of the addendum's design, it is pinned by an explicit assertion rather than argued, and matchHistoryViewerChain.ts:163 is the precedent (this surface already treats the host as the GM audience for lineage). If the owner wants the GM read narrowed to the private record only, that is a service-shaped change (a second, private-only entrypoint), not a route tweak

PRIVACY: the route accepts a caller-named ref. A ref that belongs to ANOTHER match is denied the payload by the repository's session check and is then answered by the service's non-oracle fallback with the payload-free {opaqueRef, payloadState, recordKind} view - which confirms that a record with that ref exists and what kind it is. Opaque refs are unguessable and the caller must already hold a bearer scoped to the match in the URL, but the shape is an existence oracle for a ref the caller somehow already knows. The addendum directs that this be measured and pinned, not guarded; it is measured, pinned, and raised here for the ruling

The GM receives its own draft back over HTTP for the first time. Everything E2E-19 asserts about player artifacts is unchanged, but the draft now has an authenticated read path that did not exist before, so retention and erasure behaviour (retentionClass 'session') becomes observable to a client rather than only to the server

The preview 200 body grows a new key. src/__tests__/api/matches/rewindPreviewRoute.test.ts:486 asserts the body's exact shape, so that row must change in the same head - a reviewer should read that diff as a contract change, not as a loosened test
No client reads either the new key or the new route on this head, so nothing proves the end-to-end GM flow in a browser. E2E-19's row stays a later R6.umbrella unit
